text: Database-level and routine-level privilege viewing and editing.
List supported storage engines.
Per-engine details and variables.
InnoDB status and variables page.
Plugin list grouped by type; sorting done in UI.
Charsets and collations with defaults flagged.
Keep server-level SQL, export and import entry points; PHP script lists, plugin-load errors and offset/timeout form params go; use DBLoom registry.
Keep live status charting inputs (numeric status variables, server time); OS name via PHP SysInfo and config host check replaced by adapter capability.
Keep slow/general log time-range queries and aggregation; validate time bounds properly and use log_output table sources via adapter.
Per-hour/minute/second rates and percentage per Com_ counter remain useful.
Keep global/session variable list, filter and edit; drop PHP static editable list and legacy error strings, guard SET GLOBAL by privilege.
Keep replication flag and size statistics per database; use Strategy for status statements and drop legacy pos/sort handling.
Keep engine list and InnoDB status/buffer pool pages; drop PBMS special case and unknown-engine rendering quirks.
Keep plugin list grouped by type; drop PHP anchor/tablesorter details and DisableIS handling.
Keep privilege flags per level; derive set from MySQL 8.4/MariaDB 10.11 capabilities via Strategy, include dynamic privileges.
Keep editing privileges via REVOKE/GRANT per scope; avoid tolerated-failure sequence, GRANT OPTION via WITH only on MariaDB, escape all identifiers.
Keep REQUIRE and resource limit options; drop pre-8.0.11 GRANT OPTION in WITH variant.
Revoke all privileges at a scope remains needed; escape handling stays.
Keep add-user with host choices and duplicate check; drop old_passwords and PASSWORD() logic, per-profile account vs DB account distinction.
Keep copy/rename user incl. privileges; fix column-privilege defect, use SHOW CREATE USER style, drop user-group copy unless groups kept.
Keep initial filter and show-all user list; query via adapter, not pma-specific user table assumptions.
Keep batched typed data points with name allowlist; implement as JSON API, OS metrics only where available.
Show a not-loaded state instead of computing on missing data.
Keep paged lists with has previous/next; page size from DBLoom settings instead of MaxRows config.
Reject empty selection and report pluralized success count.
Warn about anonymous localhost account blocking other hosts.
Keep allowlisting of identifiers, sort columns and flush targets; use schema validation and fix unvalidated binlog log and sort_order.
Keep binlog event viewer; TableNavigationLinksMode preference dropped, use standard pagination UI.
Keep success message with SQL and navigation to new database; no global $db clearing, return error cleanly.
Optional create-database-per-user and wildcard grants remain useful, only after successful account creation.
Keep log-name allowlist and additionally validate/escape name in SQL; fix legacy defect.
Use IDENTIFIED BY / WITH plugin with escaped value on all supported servers; drop SELECT PASSWORD() and version branches.
Mask passwords in displayed and logged SQL while executing real value.
Keep capability detection (can read mysql.user, grant, create user) but via adapter and not session cache; informs UI only.
Keep keep/none/userdefined choices, confirmation and masked display; passwords via parameterized/escaped APIs, never logged.
Do not copy listed weaknesses; validate plugin names, sort order, binlog name, skip count as integer, protect replication credentials.
Keep section, text, alerts-only and no-format filters on status variables; categories only if populated.
Progress column only on MariaDB, via adapter capability.
Byte variables shown raw and humanized; escape non-numeric values.
Lock and unlock accounts with success/error feedback; MySQL 8.4 and MariaDB 10.11 support ACCOUNT LOCK.
Export of user privileges as GRANT statements from list and user page.
Keep create form with charset/collation choice and default marked; permission-gated by server privileges, ShowCreateDb/MaxDbList config dropped.
Live monitor chart grid is a whole feature; owner decides. If kept, refresh rates and grid defaults would be redesigned. (owner decision 2026-10-23, feature: server monitor)
Keep optional auto-refresh of process list with selectable interval; implement with client polling, no PHP-style POST/abort mechanics.
Keep: never show view totals as exact; make the view count cap a DBLoom setting instead of MaxExactCountViews.
Keep data-only copy not creating target table; drop the config-storage duplication part.
Persisted bookmarks, SQL history and saved searches are a feature choice; la_ tables replaced by DBLoom own storage. (owner decision 2026-10-23, feature: bookmarks and history)
Index type model (primary, unique, index, spatial, fulltext) and loading from information_schema still needed.
Keep MySQL vs MariaDB branching via Strategy (ARCH-TGT-002); drop checks for versions below MySQL 8.4 / MariaDB 10.11.
Respect lower_case_table_names when creating or renaming databases and tables.
Keep parse, limit, run, count, render flow as an adapter-based pipeline; not PHP controller structure.
Keep default SELECT * browse with optional primary key order; drop bookmark-as-default-query behaviour.
Keep automatic paging LIMIT only for safe SELECTs; page sizes become DBLoom settings.
Total row count via COUNT over the unlimited query, skipped when page is not full.
Use approximate table count and exact count only below threshold; threshold configurable.
Clamp page position after deletes and also for out-of-range browse requests; avoid error-suppression defect.
Remember per-table sort order, stored in DBLoom user preferences instead of config-storage table properties.
Show SHOW WARNINGS output after executed statements.
Distinguish views from tables; view counts unknown or capped with a lower-bound notice; no data copy for views.
Keep rows per page, long-text truncation and repeated headers as DBLoom preferences, not PHP session tmpval.
Relational column dropdown with browse fallback for large referenced tables in inline edit.
Keep query timing; profiling via SHOW PROFILE is deprecated, use performance_schema or EXPLAIN ANALYZE where available.
Keep running multiple statements with custom delimiter; implement in DBLoom SQL runner and import, not via PHP import route.
Keep optional transaction wrapper for DML on transactional tables with rollback; implement via explicit transaction in a connection.
Show server error with failing SQL; optional continue-on-error for multi-statement runs; no mysqlDie page.
Saving executed queries as bookmarks (replace, all-users) is part of the bookmark feature decision. (owner decision 2026-10-23, feature: bookmarks and history)
Bookmark placeholder variables only matter if bookmarks are adopted. (owner decision 2026-10-23, feature: bookmarks and history)
SQL history stays useful; store per user in DBLoom storage with a configurable cap, not PHP session or la_history.
Render all result sets from routine calls and report affected rows.
Database rename and copy including routines, views, events, triggers and FK handling; no DELIMITER client syntax.
Reject empty or identical target names; apply lower_case_table_names rule.
Offer switching to the new database after copy as an in-app navigation choice, not a persisted session flag.
Optional privilege adjustment on copy/rename remains useful; use MySQL 8.4 / MariaDB 10.11 grant tables only.
Generate and execute CREATE TABLE from columns, keys, partitions and options.
Keep name syntax validation but also enforce the 64-character identifier limit client-side.
Second review (Haiku, 10 reviewers, 2026-10-23): RENAME TABLE for tables and views stays; the configuration-storage updates are dropped.
Try native RENAME TABLE first, fall back to copy only on failure.
Keep structure, constraint, index and auto-increment copy steps; drop export-plugin based implementation.
Copy data with NO_AUTO_VALUE_ON_ZERO, non-generated columns only, nothing for views or structure-only.
Second review (Haiku, 10 reviewers, 2026-10-23): copying column transformations with a copied table stays (DBLoom store); internal relations are deferred with the designer.
Keep DROP VIEW vs DROP TABLE per object type; drop config-storage cleanup.
Truncate selected tables, skip views, with confirmation.
Optionally disable FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS for destructive operations and restore the prior value.
Add one or more columns via ALTER TABLE ADD, combined with creation flows.
Keep alter-table options (engine, collation, row format, auto-increment, comment); engine-specific options gated by server product.
Keep column metadata for forms from information_schema; reserved-name reporting for pma tables dropped.
Create, edit and drop indexes with validation errors (PRIMARY naming rules); edit drops old index in same ALTER.
Report redundant duplicate indexes as notices.
Native InnoDB FK add/change/drop with RESTRICT default.
Create/alter views with algorithm, definer, security, check option.
Drop/alter views; no backup step needed.
Routine browse/create/edit/execute/drop; DBLoom uses own form/SQL building.
Routine execute dialog with parameters and result sets.
Trigger create/edit/drop with validation.
